fluxes.title: Sugars flow from leaves to roots
fluxes.text: Trees send part of the carbon they fix in their needles down to their roots, and much of it continues into the fungi that live on those roots.

fluxes.title: Roots feed their fungal partners
fluxes.text: Mycorrhizal fungi live on plant carbon and in return extend a web of fine threads through soil far beyond the reach of the roots themselves.

fluxes.title: Fungi return nitrogen and phosphorus
fluxes.text: In temperate and boreal forests, mycorrhizal fungi and nitrogen-fixing bacteria are estimated to supply up to 80% of the nitrogen and up to 75% of the phosphorus that plants take up each year, which makes the soil community a working part of the forest’s own growth.

fluxes.title: Fungi build long-term soil carbon
fluxes.text: On forested islands in northern Sweden, 50 to 70% of the carbon stored in the soil came from roots and root-associated fungi, a finding that moved fungi to the centre of how forest soils hold carbon.

fluxes.title: Fungal threads bind soil into crumbs
fluxes.text: Fungal hyphae entangle soil particles and their secretions help glue them into stable aggregates, the crumb structure that leaves pores open for air and water.

fluxes.title: A diverse soil community holds nutrients in place
fluxes.text: When experiments simplified soil communities, several functions declined together, among them nutrient retention, nutrient cycling and decomposition, which links the diversity of soil life directly to how much the soil keeps and how much it loses.

fluxes.title: Water soaks in and leaves slowly
fluxes.text: Well-structured forest soil lets rain and snowmelt soak in and drain through the ground, so what reaches a stream arrives later and carries less soil and fewer dissolved nutrients.

fluxes.title: Nitrate pulses into the stream
fluxes.text: When every tree in a small New Hampshire watershed was cut and regrowth suppressed, stream nitrate rose about 41-fold in the first year and 56-fold in the second, and streamflow rose by roughly 39%, because the living roots that had been taking up nitrogen and water were gone.
fluxes.where: Hubbard Brook, New Hampshire · experimental clearcut

fluxes.title: Dissolved carbon reaches treatment plants
fluxes.text: Colorado treatment plants drawing from watersheds hit by the mountain pine beetle recorded more total organic carbon and more disinfection byproducts, which form when that carbon meets chlorine, and the increase tracked the extent of tree death upstream.

fluxes.title: Sediment and debris fill a reservoir
fluxes.text: After the Buffalo Creek and Hayman fires burned in the South Platte watershed, storms carried sediment and debris into Denver Water’s supply, and the utility reports spending more than US$27 million on cleanup and repairs before it began investing in forest health upstream.

forage.text: Across 23 studies of 16 crops on five continents, visits by native pollinators fell to half their near-habitat level about 0.6 km from natural habitat, and pollinator richness fell by half at about 1.5 km.

network.text: Each circle is a habitat patch and each line a gap that a disperser can cross. The network is illustrative, built to show the stepping-stone role that the Eagle parcel might play, while the real habitat network around the parcel remains unmapped.

ledger.elsewhere: A survey of 27 U.S. water suppliers found treatment and chemical costs about 20% lower for every 10% more forest in the source watershed, up to about 60% cover, with forest cover explaining roughly half of the variation in cost. In Colorado, plants below beetle-killed forest saw more disinfection byproducts.
ledger.here: No intake traced from the parcel and no utility named.

ledger.elsewhere: Denver Water reports more than US$27 million spent after the Buffalo Creek and Hayman fires, and its From Forests to Faucets partners have committed more than US$96 million to forest work upstream since 2010.
ledger.here: No fire, erosion or sediment record exists for the parcel.

ledger.elsewhere: Forest near Costa Rican coffee raised yields by 20% within 1 km, and crops that depend on animal pollination supply about 35% of global production volume.
ledger.here: No pollinator is recorded and no flowering crop or garden has been mapped within flight range.

ledger.pathway: Water quantity and quality along the Colorado
ledger.elsewhere: The Colorado River and its tributaries supply municipal water to nearly 40 million people, an estimate that independent analysts place nearer 35 million, and irrigate nearly 4.5 million acres.
ledger.here: Delivery from the parcel to the Eagle River, and from there to any user, is untraced.

ledger.elsewhere: Corridors increased movement between habitat patches by about 50% across 78 experiments, they carried pollen and seeds between patches in a landscape-scale trial, and fragmentation experiments lowered biodiversity by 13 to 75%.
ledger.here: The habitat network around the parcel is unmapped, so its role as a stepping stone is unknown.
